resources.string: See who contributed to Mumla (web link)
Minimum volume level for detecting voice (when transmit mode is \"Voice activity\").
Use a physical button to transmit audio.
Press a screen corner to transmit audio throughout Android.
Change the look of the app.
Preferred audio sample rate. Some devices support fewer rates.
Prefilled name used when adding a server, or connecting to a public server.
Generates a new self-signed Mumla certificate. Recommended for beginners.
Turn off Opus support for Mumble 1.2.4 servers.
Removes background noise from your microphone before it is sent.
How deeply the Speex denoiser cuts. Only used while noise suppression is set to Light.
Also use your phone\'s own noise suppression effect on the microphone.
Also use your phone\'s own automatic gain control on the microphone.
The other controls in this section depend on this choice.

Where the threshold sits between the measured background noise and your measured voice. Higher means you have to be clearer above the room; lower lets more through. The bar below shows both marks moving.
Keeps measuring how loud the room is and moves the threshold with it. Switch off to set the level by hand.
The room level the threshold is measured from, in dB below full scale. Only used while "Follow the background noise" is off.
Forgets what has been learned about the room and your voice, and starts measuring from scratch.
How long a sound has to last before it counts as speech. Longer settings keep single keyboard clicks out; each step costs 10 ms of the beginning of a word.
Keep sending this long after your voice drops below the threshold, so pauses inside a sentence are not cut.
Speech probability at which sending starts.
Speech probability below which sending stops.
Since this version the level is measured after noise suppression, so an old setting means a different volume than it used to. "Automatic" needs no calibration.
Live microphone level with the background and threshold marks.
Microphone unavailable — permission missing, or another app is using it.
Your voice is barely above the room. Move closer to the phone or make it quieter.
Plays your processed voice back while this is on. Use headphones — over the loudspeaker this will howl.
Only useful if you use Push-to-talk corner or physical key.
Read incoming message aloud using speech synthesis.
Shorten the messages by only reading the domain names of links.
Push-to-talk button toggles transmission on/off. No need to hold it.
Re-establishes connection to server when lost.
Preferred rate of data transmitted (in bits per second).
Change the vertical length of the push-to-talk button.
Press a physical key to use it for push-to-talk.
The app must be open to use this (due to Android restrictions).
Downloads and shows pictures in chat.
Remove all trusted server certificates from Mumla.
Mutes other playback during push-to-talk to avoid audio loops/feedback.
Uses the front speaker and proximity sensor to simulate a traditional phone call.
Play sound effect when pressing the push-to-talk button.
Suppresses ambient noise and normalizes audio volume.
The length of audio per voice packet.
Keeps the screen on when Mumla is open.
The default to use when connecting to a server.
Shows the number of users in channel subtrees.
Enables \"Pinned channels\" mode after connecting (hides channels that are not pinned).

What the play/pause button of a wired or Bluetooth headset does while you are connected, including when the screen is off. Tap it: a button you hold down does nothing at all, because Android gives a long press to the voice assistant. And it toggles — one tap switches on, the next switches off — while the on-screen and physical push-to-talk keys transmit only as long as you hold them, unless \"Sticky Push-to-talk button\" is on.
Nothing — leave the media keys to your music app
Toggle push-to-talk, or mute in the other transmit modes

Send and receive voice through a connected Bluetooth headset while you are connected to a server, and switch to a headset that connects during the call. The audio device can be changed for the call from the channel menu. Asks for the Nearby devices permission; some devices will not route audio to a headset without it.
